summary: The Measure tool now prints the same key, I, on every screen of the design study, and that is the key the app actually binds. The eyedropper, which shares Photoshop's I group, prints its shifted sibling ⇧I everywhere it prints a key at all.
setup: The design study at http://127.0.0.1:8791. No app change, so Photonz Dev looks the same as before: this is about what the mocks teach.

try.do: Open http://127.0.0.1:8791/index.html#lang-keyboard and read the Tools column of the legend.
Read the rule text beside it, block 04, the paragraph starting "Two tools that share one of Photoshop's groups".
Open http://127.0.0.1:8791/index.html#redline and hover the ruler button in the tool strip.
Open http://127.0.0.1:8791/index.html#icon-gradient-wt and hover the eyedropper, then the ruler two buttons to its right.
On that same page open the More tools overflow menu and read the same two rows.
Open http://127.0.0.1:8791/index.html#color and hover the eyedropper in the color picker header.

evaluate: Reading only the legend, would you press I for the ruler without hesitating?
The eyedropper inside a color picker now says ⇧I. Does that read as a real keystroke you could press there, or as noise on a button you were going to click anyway?
Photoshop opens its I group on the eyedropper and files the ruler behind it. Photonz does the reverse. Does putting measuring first feel right for this app?
In the icon page's tool strip the eyedropper and the ruler sit two buttons apart with I and ⇧I. Do they read as two members of one family, or as two unrelated tools with confusingly similar keys?
rough: The eyedropper in a color picker header is not really the ruler's toolbar sibling: it is a sampler inside a popover that happens to share Photoshop's group. It prints ⇧I anyway, because printing bare I there would contradict the ruler on the very same screen. Best available answer, not an obviously right one.
In the legend's Tools column, Sample a color is long enough to wrap onto two lines. Brush size and Zoom out already do the same, so it matches, but it is the longest label there.
Nothing in the app changed. A person playtesting Photonz Next will see no difference; the win is that a person learning a shortcut from a mock now learns the one the app obeys.

Found while sweeping and filed separately, not fixed here: every tool button in the study loses its accessible name when the tooltip upgrade moves title into data-tip, so a screen reader announces plain "button".
